I work on the mathematics and analytics of energy markets, with a focus on renewables, and more broadly on data science, forecasting and optimisation, with applications in energy, weather, logistics and shipping, and business analytics.

In October 2026 I joined [inCommodities](https://incommodities.com/), a Denmark-based energy trading company, as Principal, to lead research and translation. I remain a Professor at [Imperial College London](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/), in the [Dyson School of Design Engineering](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/design-engineering/). I am also Chief Scientific Advisor at Halfspace, a data and AI company in Copenhagen that was acquired by Accenture in 2025 and is now part of Faculty, and Editor-in-Chief of the [International Journal of Forecasting](ijf.qmd). Until 2026 I was a scientific advisor to and angel investor in Atmo, an AI-based weather forecasting company acquired by Vaisala.

I am an IEEE Fellow, an INFORMS member and a director of the International Institute of Forecasters. I have been on the Clarivate Highly Cited Researchers list (cross-field) in 2019–2023 and 2025, for work in statistics, meteorology, economics and power and energy engineering. In 2024 I led the team, with Halfspace and Molslinjen, that won the INFORMS Franz Edelman Award for achievement in operations research, analytics and management science. In March 2026 I gave the Ørsted Lecture at the Technical University of Denmark, a yearly public lecture often given by Nobel laureates.

Before Imperial, I spent many years at the Technical University of Denmark, as Professor of Energy Analytics and Markets and then of Operations Research. I have been a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford (Mathematical Institute) and the University of Washington (Department of Statistics), a visiting professor at École Normale Supérieure de Rennes, and a Simons Fellow at the Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences in Cambridge. I also spent a year as a scientist at the [European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts](https://www.ecmwf.int/) (ECMWF), the world's leading organisation for global weather forecasting.

What has interested me most is how to generate optimal value from data, for society and for the stakeholders involved. That brings together data science, analytics, operations research and management science, game theory and mechanism design. Some of the work I am known for includes probabilistic forecasting and forecast verification, peer-to-peer and community-based electricity markets, coordination of energy markets, and collaborative and market-based analytics such as data and analytics markets.

- [2006 – 2008]{.when} Postdoctoral Fellow, then Assistant Professor, Technical University of Denmark, Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science
